arxiv-1611-00138.title: MusicMood: Predicting the mood of music from song lyrics using machine learning
arxiv-1611-00138.creator: Sebastian Raschka
arxiv-1611-00138.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Sebastian Raschka. Sentiment prediction of contemporary music can have a wide-range of applications in modern society, for instance, selecting music for public institutions such as hospitals or restaurants to potentially improve the emotional well-being of personnel, patients, and customers, respectively. In this project, music recommendation system built upon on a naive Bayes classifier, trained to predict the sentiment of songs based on song lyrics alone.

arxiv-2111-02905.title: Non-equilibrium Photoionization and Hydrodynamic Simulations of Starburst-driven Outflows
arxiv-2111-02905.creator: A Danehkar, M S Oey and W J Gray
arxiv-2111-02905.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by A Danehkar, M S Oey and W J Gray. Starburst-driven galactic outflows in star-forming galaxies have been observed to contain complex thermal structures and emission line features that are difficult to explain by adiabatic fluid models and plasmas in photoionization equilibrium (PIE) and collisional ionization equilibrium (CIE). We previously performed hydrodynamic simulations of starburst-driven outflows using the maihem module for non-equilibrium atomic chemistry and radiative cooling functions in the hydrodynamics code flash , and calculated emission lines in combined CIE and PIE conditions.

arxiv-2111-06282.title: Compositions and decompositions of binary relations
arxiv-2111-06282.creator: Ivan Chajda, Helmut Länger
arxiv-2111-06282.description: Abstract It is well-known that to every binary relation on a non-void set I I there can be assigned its incidence matrix, also in the case when I I is infinite. We show that a certain kind of “multiplication” of such incidence matrices corresponds to the composition of the corresponding relations.

arxiv-2201-00345.title: Robust Algorithmic Collusion
arxiv-2201-00345.creator: Nicolas Eschenbaum, Filip Mellgren, Philipp Zahn
arxiv-2201-00345.description: Abstract This paper develops a formal framework to assess policies of learning algorithms in economic games. We investigate whether reinforcement-learning agents with collusive pricing policies can successfully extrapolate collusive behavior from training to the market. We find that in testing environments collusion consistently breaks down. Instead, we observe static Nash play.

arxiv-2302-12696.title: A realistic coalescence model for deuteron production
arxiv-2302-12696.creator: Maximilian Mahlein, Luca Barioglio, Francesca Bellini, Laura Fabbietti, Chiara Pinto, Bhawani Singh, Sushanta Tripathy
arxiv-2302-12696.description: Abstract A microscopic understanding of (anti)deuteron production in hadron-hadron collisions is the subject of many experimental and theoretical efforts in nuclear physics. This topic is also very relevant for astrophysics, since the rare production of antinuclei in our Universe could be a doorway to discover new physics.

arxiv-2403-16625.title: A perfect obstruction theory for 𝐒𝐔 ⁡ ( 2 ) \mathbf{SU}(2) -Higgs sheaves
arxiv-2403-16625.creator: Simon Schirren
arxiv-2403-16625.description: Abstract Abstract. We present a new method for constructing virtual cycles for rank-2 Higgs sheaves (E,\phi) on a smooth projective surface S . Using this, we redefine the \mathbf{SU}(2) -perfect obstruction theory previously constructed by Tanaka-Thomas. The key step in our construction involves modifying the \mathbf{C}^{\times} -localisation formula of Graber-Pandharipande by replacing the torus action with an involution (E,\phi)\mapsto(E^{*},-\phi^{*}) .

arxiv-2405-20248.title: Image-to-Joint Inverse Kinematic of a Supportive Continuum Arm Using Deep Learning Thanks:
arxiv-2405-20248.creator: Shayan Sepahvand, Guanghui Wang, Farrokh Janabi-Sharifi
arxiv-2405-20248.description: Abstract In this work, a deep learning-based technique is used to study the image-to-joint inverse kinematics of a tendon-driven supportive continuum arm. An eye-off-hand configuration is considered by mounting a camera at a fixed pose with respect to the inertial frame attached at the arm base.

arxiv-2504-00934.title: InformGen: An AI Copilot for Accurate and Compliant Clinical Research Consent Document Generation
arxiv-2504-00934.creator: Zifeng Wang, Junyi Gao, Benjamin Danek, Brandon Theodorou, Ruba Shaik, Shivashankar Thati, Seunghyun Won, Jimeng Sun
arxiv-2504-00934.description: Abstract Leveraging large language models (LLMs) to generate high-stakes documents, such as informed consent forms (ICFs), remains a significant challenge due to the extreme need for regulatory compliance and factual accuracy. Here, we present InformGen, an LLM-driven copilot for accurate and compliant ICF drafting by optimized knowledge document parsing and content generation, with humans in the loop.

arxiv-2506-10627.title: NeuralNexus at BEA 2025 Shared Task: Retrieval-Augmented Prompting for Mistake Identification in AI Tutors
arxiv-2506-10627.creator: Numaan Naeem, Sarfraz Ahmad, Momina Ahsan, Hasan Iqbal
arxiv-2506-10627.description: Abstract This paper presents our system for Track 1: Mistake Identification in the BEA 2025 Shared Task on Pedagogical Ability Assessment of AI-powered Tutors . The task involves evaluating whether a tutor’s response correctly identifies a mistake in a student’s mathematical reasoning.

arxiv-2511-01001.title: Towards Portability at Scale: A Cross-Architecture Performance Evaluation of a GPU-enabled Shallow Water Solver
arxiv-2511-01001.creator: Johansell Villalobos 1 - jovillalobos@cenat.ac.cr, Daniel Caviedes-Voullième 2 3 - d.caviedes.voullieme@fz-juelich.de, Silvio Rizzi 4 - srizzi@anl.gov, Esteban Meneses 1 5 - emeneses@cenat.ac.cr
arxiv-2511-01001.description: Abstract Current climate change has posed a grand challenge in the field of numerical modeling due to its complex, multiscale dynamics. In hydrological modeling, the increasing demand for high-resolution, real-time simulations has led to the adoption of GPU-accelerated platforms and performance portable programming frameworks such as Kokkos.

arxiv-2601-00680.title: Sigmoid Head for Quality Estimation under Language Ambiguity
arxiv-2601-00680.creator: Tu Anh Dinh, Jan Niehues
arxiv-2601-00680.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Tu Anh Dinh, Jan Niehues. Language model (LM) probability is not a reliable quality estimator, as natural language is ambiguous. When multiple output options are valid, the model’s probability distribution is spread across them, which can misleadingly indicate low output quality.

arxiv-2601-20084.title: IMRNNs: An Efficient Method for Interpretable Dense Retrieval via Embedding Modulation
arxiv-2601-20084.creator: Yash Saxena, Ankur Padia, Kalpa Gunaratna, Manas Gaur
arxiv-2601-20084.description: Abstract Interpretability in black-box dense retrievers remains a central challenge in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Understanding how queries and documents semantically interact is critical for diagnosing retrieval behavior and improving model design. However, existing dense retrievers rely on static embeddings for both queries and documents, which obscures this bidirectional relationship.

pmc-10615067.title: Assessing the measurement properties of life-space mobility measures in community-dwelling older adults: a systematic review
pmc-10615067.creator: Ayse Kuspinar, Ava Mehdipour, Marla K Beauchamp, Qiukui Hao, Emily Cino, Christopher Mikton, Jotheeswaran Amuthavalli Thiyagarajan, Theresa Diaz, Parminder Raina

Life-space mobility is a construct that captures actual mobility within the home and the community. The objective of this systematic review was to synthesise the measurement properties and interpretability of scores produced by life-space mobility measures in community-dwelling older adults.

pmc-11456784.title: Penile superficial dorsal vein thrombophlebitis following prolonged sexual activity
pmc-11456784.creator: Ahmed Adam Osman, Hanan HassanHirei, Abdulkadir Isse Mohamed, Shuayb Moallim Ali, Amal Naleye Ali, Abdikarim Hussein Mohamed
pmc-11456784.description: Penile Mondor disease (MD) is a palpable, painful, subcutaneous induration resulting from thrombosis of the superficial dorsal penile vein. In this report, we present a 53-year-old case of Mondor disease following prolonged, vigorous sexual activity. He had engaged in sexual activity the previous night after taking sildenafil.

pmc-11665825.title: Increase of niche filling with increase of host richness for plant-infecting mastreviruses
pmc-11665825.creator: Sélim Ben Chéhida, Heemee Devi Bunwaree, Murielle Hoareau, Oumaima Moubset, Charlotte Julian, Laurence Blondin, Denis Filloux, Christophe Lavergne, Philippe Roumagnac, Arvind Varsani, Darren P Martin, Jean-Michel Lett, Pierre Lefeuvre
pmc-11665825.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Now that it has been realized that viruses are ubiquitous, questions have been raised on factors influencing their diversity and distribution. For phytoviruses, understanding the interplay between plant diversity and virus species richness and prevalence remains cardinal. As both the amplification and the dilution of viral species richness due to increasing host diversity have been theorized and observed, a deeper understanding of how plants and viruses interact in natural environments is needed to explore how host availability conditions viral diversity and distributions.

pmc-12570515.title: Impact of different 3D culture environments on spheroid morphology, drug response, and invasion in pancreatic cancer cells
pmc-12570515.creator: Didem Karakas, Sila Sigirli
pmc-12570515.description: ObjectiveThree-dimensional (3D) culture systems offer a more physiologically relevant environment than conventional two-dimensional (2D) cultures, particularly for studying tumor biology. Here, we systematically compared two widely used 3D platforms—poly(2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate) (Poly-HEMA, PH)-coating and ultra-low attachment (ULA) plates—to evaluate their impact on pancreatic cancer (PCa) cell behavior.

pmc-12623943.title: Profiling of vaginal microbial communities in Chilean women via self-sampling and nanopore sequencing
pmc-12623943.creator: Barbara Oliva-Arancibia, Pablo Villanueva, Juan A Ugalde
pmc-12623943.description: The vaginal microbiota is a dynamic ecosystem that plays a central role in women’s reproductive health, with Lactobacillus species typically dominating in healthy individuals. Disruptions to this microbiota can lead to dysbiosis, increasing susceptibility to infections such as bacterial vaginosis and contributing to adverse reproductive outcomes.

pmc-13146902.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1438 TRIPTAN EXPOSURE AFTER ISCHAEMIC STROKE OR MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION: A RETROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY
pmc-13146902.creator: Georg Royl, Anna Cirkel, Elena Rakusa, Michelle Oswald, Nils Werring, Ralf J Ludwig, Jens Minnerup, Tobias Wagner-Altendorf
pmc-13146902.description: Background and aimsTriptans are a mainstay of acute migraine therapy but are contraindicated after ischaemic stroke (IS) or myocardial infarction (MI) because of presumed vasoconstrictive effects. However, evidence for increased vascular risk after triptan exposure in these populations is limited. We assessed whether triptan use after IS or MI is associated with recurrent vascular events in patients with migraine.

pmc-13556464.title: 541. Serum neurofilament light chain is associated with psychotic remission, independent of antipsychotic treatment in schizophrenia
pmc-13556464.creator: P-Y Chen, M-C Huang
pmc-13556464.description: BackgroundSchizophrenia involves neuroaxonal disruption linked to psychotic symptoms and clinical remission. Blood neurofilament light chain (NfL), a neuronal scaffolding protein essential for axonal integrity and synaptic activity, is released into the cerebrospinal fluid and blood upon neurodegeneration. Often described as a "troponin for the brain," NfL was recently FDA-approved as a surrogate endpoint for neuroaxonal injury.
